title: From archive to resource: bringing legacy data back to life at scale with large language models
abstract: arXiv:2610.32616v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Pharmaceutical companies maintain vast archives of legacy preclinical study reports that contain study-context details, such as fasting, anesthesia, and laboratory instrumentation, that are rarely captured in structured data formats, yet they can correlate with clinical pathology parameters values and limit the reuse of historical data. This work demonstrates practical, scalable solutions to recover such descriptors from heterogeneous report texts using large language model (LLM)-based extraction pipelines developed independently by two industry teams. The pipelines identify and normalize metadata fields and return verbatim evidence with page and section reference, hasting human verification and iterative refinement. Evaluation of over 400 documents against expert-curated reference values showed high agreement across a broad set of metadata fields. translated_title: 从档案到资源：利用大语言模型大规模盘活遗留数据
translated_abstract: 制药公司拥有大量遗留的临床前研究报告档案，其中包含研究背景细节，如禁食、麻醉和实验室仪器等信息。这些信息很少以结构化数据格式保存，但它们可能与临床病理学参数值相关联，并限制历史数据的重复利用。这项工作展示了实用且可扩展的解决方案：由两个行业团队独立开发的基于大语言模型（LLM）的提取流水线，能够从异构的报告文本中恢复此类描述符。这些流水线可以识别和规范化元数据字段，并返回带有页码和章节引用的逐字证据，从而加速人工验证和迭代改进。对超过400份文档对照专家整理的参考值进行评估，结果显示在广泛的元数据字段范围内具有高度一致性。对于报告方式一致的项目表现最佳，而对于（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究由两个行业团队独立开发基于大语言模型的提取流水线，从制药公司遗留的临床前研究报告档案中大规模恢复禁食、麻醉等 rarely captured 的研究背景描述符，并返回带页码引用的逐字证据，对400多份文档的评估显示与专家参考值高度一致，有效实现了历史数据的再利用。
en_tdlr: Two independently developed LLM-based extraction pipelines recover rarely-structured study-context metadata (e.g., fasting, anesthesia, lab instrumentation) from legacy preclinical study reports at scale, returning verbatim evidence with page references and showing high agreement with expert-curated reference values across 400+ documents.
